title: Bay County public records, mapped
description: Maps, money and public records for Bay County, Florida, with a source on every figure.
lede: Trash day and schools, beaches and storms, your tax bill and who decides how it's spent. Every figure links to its source.

title: My Address
description: Look up any Bay County address: property tax estimate, who represents you, zoned schools, flood and evacuation zones, and whether it is in a redevelopment district.
lede: Type a Bay County street address to see your property tax estimate, who represents you, your schools, your flood and evacuation zones, and whether you're inside a redevelopment district.

explainer.heading: How this works
paragraphs: Addresses, parcels, property values and district boundaries come live from Bay County's public GIS server, which publishes the Property Appraiser's parcel data. Property values are the 2026 roll. Flood zones come live from FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer, the official current flood map, with the FIRM panel and any map revision (LOMR) that applies.

The tax estimate applies the rates adopted in September 2026 (FY2027 bills; sources on the Tax Dollars page) to the 2026 values. The NW Florida Water Management District and Beach Mosquito Control District rates for 2026 were not found yet, so their 2025 rates are used. Flat non-ad valorem fees (fire, stormwater, lighting and similar) come from the Florida Department of Revenue's parcel-level file for the 2025 tax roll, so they show what was on the FY2026 bill. For a homestead, school tax is figured on the value before the second homestead exemption, since that one doesn't apply to schools. Other exemptions are taken as reported by the Property Appraiser. Your official bill comes from the Tax Collector.

title: CRA Spending
description: Interactive map and ledger of Bay County, Florida's six Community Redevelopment Agencies: who was paid, where, and for what.
lede: Every Community Redevelopment Agency in Bay County, mapped on the county's official district boundaries, with the payments, grants, contracts and budget lines found in public records: who got paid, where, and for what.

explainer.heading: What's a CRA?
paragraphs: A Community Redevelopment Agency is like a savings jar for one neighborhood that needs fixing up.
Why it matters: every dollar in the jar is a dollar the city and county don't have for everything else. This page shows what each jar paid for.

title: How much property tax goes to the CRAs
description: How much property tax Bay County and the cities pay to the six Community Redevelopment Agencies each year (seven tax-increment areas), who pays it, what has been paid so far and what it could add up to before each CRA ends, with the method and the missing years.
lede: Six Community Redevelopment Agencies in Bay County collect tax increment, in seven areas (Panama City Beach has two, Front Beach Road and Pier Park): the property tax that Bay County and the cities levy on growth in value inside each district since its base year. Here is how much that is each year, who pays it, what has been paid so far and what it could add up to before each CRA ends.

title: How your tax dollars are allocated
description: Estimate your Bay County property tax bill and see who gets each slice, plus where the county, schools and every city get their money and what they spend it on.
lede: Your property tax bill isn't one tax. It's several governments each taking a slice. Here's who gets what from your bill, where each government's other money comes from, and what it pays for.

explainer.heading: How a property tax bill works
paragraphs: Each of these governments is a taxing authority. Rates here are for fiscal year FY2027.

title: Amendment 3: what changes in Bay County
description: What Florida's 2026 Amendment 3 would do to Bay County property tax bills and local budgets, using the state's own estimates. Before-and-after calculator; both sides' arguments; no position taken.
lede: On November 3, 2026, Florida voters decide Amendment 3, a property tax change. It needs at least 60% "yes" to pass. This page shows what it would do to your bill and to local budgets here, using the state's own estimates.

title: Where the Hurricane Michael money went
description: FEMA, HUD and state recovery money in Bay County after Hurricane Michael: every FEMA project, household aid by city, Rebuild Florida awards, debris costs and the Lynn Haven case.
lede: Hurricane Michael hit Bay County on October 10, 2018. Billions in federal, state and insurance money followed. This page tracks the public part: who received it, what it paid for, and what's still unclear.

title: The bed tax: what visitors pay and where it goes
description: Bay County's 5% tourist development tax: ten years of collections by zone, how the pennies are split, what Visit Panama City Beach spends, and who decides.
lede: Visitors who rent a hotel room, condo or house for six months or less pay a 5% tourist development tax on top of sales tax. It brings in tens of millions a year, almost all from Panama City Beach, and state law limits what it can be spent on.

explainer.heading: How the bed tax works
paragraphs: State law would allow a 6th cent. Bay County doesn't levy it; the County Commission declined to add it in 2023.

title: Half-cent sales taxes: promised vs built
description: Every infrastructure sales tax project on Bay County's map with its status, the county's surtax money by year, and the school half-cent.
lede: Bay County has two extra half-cent sales taxes that voters approved: one for roads and infrastructure, one for school buildings. Here is every infrastructure project on the county's map, and what we could find about the school tax.

title: Fees on your tax bill, and utility bills
description: Fire, stormwater and other flat fees on Bay County tax bills, and a typical monthly water, sewer and garbage bill in each city.
lede: Pick where you live to see the flat fees on your yearly tax bill and a typical monthly water, sewer and garbage bill.

explainer.heading: How every area compares
paragraphs: Tax-bill fees plus 12 months of water, sewer and garbage at 5,000 gallons a month. * Garbage isn't on this utility bill, so the total leaves it out. Parker's utility rates weren't found online.

title: Bay County's local governments
description: A profile of every local government in Bay County, Florida: officials, budget, tax rate, debt, audits, votes, contracts and projects.
lede: One page for each government: who runs it, its budget and tax rate, debt, audit findings, votes, contracts and projects. Pick yours, or compare them side by side.

title: Compare Bay County governments
description: Compare Bay County, its cities and the school district side by side: budget, property tax, debt, staff, audit findings, split votes and utility bills, per resident.
lede: Pick the governments you want to see side by side. Bigger places spend and owe more, so most measures can also be shown per resident.

title: Download the data
description: Every BayCounty.me dataset as CSV and JSON: votes, contracts, CRA spending, tax rates, debt, audits, FEMA projects and more.
lede: Everything on BayCounty.me, as spreadsheets. Free to use for reporting, research or your own analysis. Please credit BayCounty.me, and check the original record before relying on any single figure: every row carries its source link.

title: My home
description: Sign in and save your home address to see what’s happening around it: alerts for your home, trash day, meetings, events, building and road work nearby, with an optional Monday email and phone notifications.
lede: Save your address once. BayCounty.me shows you the alerts, meetings, events and work going on near you, and tells you about the ones you care about by email or on your phone.

title: Realtor console: branded address reports
description: For real estate agents: type any Bay County address and download one branded PDF with the property, a tax estimate, flood and evacuation zones, schools, utilities, zoning and projects nearby, parks and who represents it.
lede: Type any Bay County address and get one report with the property, a tax estimate, flood and evacuation zones, schools, utilities, zoning and projects nearby, parks and who represents it. Download it as a PDF with your logo, colors and contact details.

title: API for developers
description: Connect apps, spreadsheets and AI assistants to BayCounty.me: a free, read-only API and MCP server for Bay County public records.
lede: Connect your own app, spreadsheet, newsroom tool or AI assistant to the public records on this site. Free, read-only, and no key needed.

title: Request a public record
description: Write a Florida public records request to any Bay County government in a minute: pick a record the site is missing or describe your own.
lede: Florida's public records law lets anyone see government records, without saying why. Pick a government and a record this site is missing, or describe your own, and we'll write the request for you.

title: Emergencies and alerts in Bay County
description: What's happening now in Bay County: National Weather Service warnings, evacuation orders, open shelters, boil-water notices and road closures, checked every few minutes. Look up the evacuation zone for any address and find every county shelter.
lede: What is happening now in Bay County: weather warnings, evacuation orders, open shelters, boil-water notices and road closures, gathered from the National Weather Service, FEMA's emergency alert system, the county and the cities every few minutes. Look up your evacuation zone, find every shelter and get alerts on your phone.

title: Hurricane prep for Bay County
description: Get ready for hurricane season in Bay County: a plan and a kit, sandbags, generator safety, what to do when a storm is coming and after it, every federal disaster declaration since 2016 and the FEMA rebuild money that reached each ZIP code.
lede: Get ready for hurricane season in Bay County: a plan and a kit, sandbags, generator safety, what to do when a storm is coming and after it passes. Plus every federal disaster declaration since 2016, and how much FEMA housing aid and flood insurance money reached each part of the county after past storms.

title: Get BayCounty.me updates by email
description: Follow Bay County, the school district or your city and get a short weekly email with new votes, data, corrections and upcoming meetings.
lede: Follow the governments you care about. Once a week, when there's something new, you'll get a short email: new votes and data, corrections, and the meetings coming up.

title: Upcoming public meetings in Bay County
description: When and where the County Commission, School Board and every city commission meet, with agenda links and the money items on each agenda.
lede: When and where every Bay County board meets, with agenda links and the money items on each agenda. Public comment is open at regular meetings; check the agenda for how to speak.

title: Campaign gifts and contracts
description: Who funded the campaigns of Bay County's current elected officials, from Supervisor of Elections reports, and which donors also hold local government contracts.
lede: Who paid for the most recent campaigns of Bay County's current elected officials, from the reports they file with the Supervisor of Elections, and which donors also hold local government contracts.

title: Compare budgets across years
description: Compare any Bay County government's budget in two fiscal years, such as Lynn Haven FY2025 and FY2026: what grew, what shrank and what's new, by department, service and fund, in dollars and percent.
lede: Pick a government and any two fiscal years to see what grew, what shrank and what's new: the total, the General Fund, each department, each service and each fund, in dollars and percent.

title: Who's running in 2026
description: Every local race on Bay County ballots in 2026: the candidates, their platforms in their own words, links to their campaigns, and where their campaign money comes from.
lede: Every local race on Bay County ballots this year: the candidates, their plans in their own words, and their campaign money. BayCounty.me doesn't endorse or rate candidates.

explainer.heading: How we did this
paragraphs: Platforms are summarized only from each candidate's own campaign website, campaign social pages or questionnaire answers they wrote, with links to each source. If we couldn't find a statement from the candidate, we say so rather than fill in from news coverage. Candidates are listed alphabetically.

Money comes from the campaign reports candidates file with the Bay County Supervisor of Elections, through the date shown. Organizations are listed by name; gifts from individual people are counted and totaled, and every name is in the linked report. Florida caps gifts to local candidates at $1,000 per person or business per election.
Sitting officials' past campaigns are on the Campaign Gifts page, and every local race from 2016 to 2025 is on Past elections.

title: Election results since 2016
description: Results of every contest on a Bay County ballot since 2016, from the Supervisor of Elections: votes for each candidate and ballot question, on Election Day, early and by mail, and turnout for every election.
lede: Every contest on a Bay County ballot since 2016, from the Supervisor of Elections' official results: who got how many votes, and how they voted (on Election Day, early or by mail).

lede: Key dates, every early voting site, each precinct's polling place, and the local races on your ballot by address. From the Bay County Supervisor of Elections.

lede: Bids, public hearings and meetings that Bay County, the School Board, the cities and other public agencies are required to announce, in one searchable list. Each links to the government that posted it.

title: Government jobs

lede: Open jobs at Bay County, Bay District Schools, the cities and the airport, from each employer's own job board, in one list. Apply on the employer's site.

title: Past local elections, 2016 to 2025
description: Every candidate who ran for a local office in Bay County from 2016 through 2025, winners and losers, with what each raised and spent and which businesses and groups gave.
lede: Every candidate who ran for a local office in Bay County from 2016 through 2025, winners and losers, and where their campaign money came from. Businesses and groups that gave are named; gifts from individual people are counted and totaled.

explainer.heading: How we did this
paragraphs: Every figure comes from the campaign reports candidates filed with the Bay County Supervisor of Elections. Raised is money plus in-kind gifts, including any loans from the candidate. Spent includes refunds and leftover money a closed campaign gave away, so it often equals what was raised.

Each campaign's itemized report was checked against the Supervisor of Elections' totals: 293 match exactly, 38 raised nothing, and 11 differ slightly (the Supervisor of Elections' totals are shown). Organizations are named as filed. A filing that coded a person as a business was corrected, so that person is counted with the individuals.
The 2026 races are on Who's running in 2026. Download this data as campaign-history and campaign-contributions-history, or use the API.

lede: Every email between BayCounty.me and Bay County’s officials and governments, start to finish: letters to officials, public records requests, and the records governments email in. Read-only, exactly as sent, with residents’ personal details hidden.

lede: Groups of businesses that list the same officer, manager or registered agent in state corporate records and each gave to the same local candidate. Each group was checked by hand against the state's records before it was listed here.

description: What's happening around Bay County in the next two months, from public calendars: the county and city calendars, the library system, the visitor bureaus and the chambers. Updated every morning.
lede: What's happening around the county, from the county and city calendars, the library system, the visitor bureaus and the chambers. One list, every town, updated every morning.

lede: What's happening this week, the public meetings on the calendar, and the votes and contracts that reached BayCounty.me last week. The same list goes out by email every Monday.

description: Every nonprofit in Bay County: what each reports to the IRS, the government money and grants that reach it, and public officials who sit on its board.

lede: Find the schools zoned for your address, see what's coming up on the school calendar, and compare every public school in Bay County: grades, students, spending and how each has changed since 2016.

title: Utilities and trash day
description: Who provides water, sewer, electricity, natural gas and garbage pickup at any Bay County address, its trash and yard waste day, holiday changes, power outage lines and what each city charges for water and sewer.

title: Chambers of commerce
description: Bay County's two chambers of commerce, the Bay County Chamber and the Panama City Beach Chamber: who sits on their boards and staff, upcoming events and programs, their IRS filings, the public money they get, and board members' businesses that do work for local governments.
lede: Bay County has two main chambers of commerce: the Bay County Chamber, which covers the whole county, and the Panama City Beach Chamber. Here is who leads them, what's coming up, the public money they get and where their boards meet local government business.

title: Beaches: flags, rip currents, water quality and access
description: Today's beach flag and rip current risk for Panama City Beach and the rest of the county's Gulf beaches, what each flag means, state water quality samples at every sampling site, and every public beach access and county beach parking lot on a map.
lede: Today's beach flag and rip current risk, what each flag means, how clean the water tested at each state sampling site, and every public beach access and county beach parking lot on one map.

description: Every public park, boat ramp and trail in Bay County: playgrounds, restrooms, sports fields, fishing piers and trails, who runs each one, a map with directions, and where to sign up for leagues and programs.
lede: Every public park, boat ramp and trail in the county, from city ball fields to state parks: what each has, who runs it, how to get there, and where to sign up for leagues and programs.

lede: How many new homes are being permitted in Bay County each year, city by city, and the commercial buildings, subdivisions and apartments working their way through planning review.

lede: State highway work under way in Bay County and what each contract costs, what the Florida Department of Transportation plans for the next five years, and the county and city road jobs paid for by the half-cent sales tax.

title: Restaurant inspections

lede: Look up any restaurant, food truck or caterer in Bay County and see what state food safety inspectors found on every visit since 2016.

lede: Bay County is home to Tyndall Air Force Base and Naval Support Activity Panama City. Here is what each base does, the latest news from the units on them, and the federal contracts that go to companies based in the county.

lede: The same company, organization or person often shows up in more than one public record: a campaign report, the minutes, an agenda, a check register, a state business filing. Each overlap lives on the page where you'd look for it; this is the summary.

paragraphs: The record says the money was actually paid out.

title: About
description: What BayCounty.me is, where its information comes from, and how to send a correction.
lede: BayCounty.me is an independent, free website and app that puts Bay County, Florida public records in one place, in plain language. It covers all nine local governments: Bay County, Bay District Schools, Panama City, Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven, Callaway, Springfield, Parker and Mexico Beach.

title: Where our data comes from
description: Every source behind BayCounty.me: each government's agenda systems, websites and documents, and every state and federal database, with links, how often we check them and how we process the records.
lede: Every figure on BayCounty.me comes from a public record. This page lists every source we take records from, for every government and every state and federal database, with the link, how we get it, how often, and what we do with it.

explainer.heading: How current each figure is
paragraphs: Many public numbers come out months or a year after the period they cover. This shows the newest period we have for each headline figure, and when the next one is usually published. Where a full 2026 figure isn't out yet, the page shows this year so far against the same months last year.
The newest period is read from the data each time the site is built. The usual release schedules were checked on Oct 29, 2026; agencies sometimes publish late. Data: data-freshness.

title: Privacy

lede: BayCounty.me doesn't sell, share or track you. There are no ads and no tracking cookies, on the website or in the iPhone and Android apps, and nothing we count can pick you out. Accounts are optional: residents can sign in to save their home, and agents to use the realtor console.

lede: City of Parker: who runs it, what it spends and owes, how its commission votes, and what the auditors found, all from public records.

explainer.heading: How complete Parker’s data is
paragraphs: Counts every fiscal year since 2016 we have a record for. Votes update live as we read each board’s minutes. Data: data-completeness and import-progress. Where our data comes from.
